Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.

I’ll first read the workspace contract and inherited rollout evidence, then use the required fish-control shelf and inspect both prescribed wake views before proposing or editing the single candidate. I’ll keep the mechanism rationale in the notes and only carry evidence-supported reusable conclusions into the guidance file.

The required skills constrain this edit to a compact body-frame feedback mechanism, not route memorization or gain-only tuning. I’m now anchoring the shelf hypotheses to the sampled scores, metrics, diagnostics, inherited notes, and the best-versus-failure visual comparison before touching the policy.

The scalar/diagnostic read shows the prefill is the strongest near-miss (`2.443L`) but it passes below the target and later exits at the lower boundary. Its acute `bearing` becomes ambiguous once the target is behind; the next visual check is testing whether this is genuinely a late steering-geometry failure rather than wake collapse.

The visual comparison supports a clean diagnosis: all four self-propel with coherent alternating wakes, but every trajectory overshoots below the target and continues toward the lower boundary; there is no cylinder wake to reject. Full-direction sensing alone (`2.493L`) and approach-energy reduction alone (`2.845L`) did not change that termination class, so I’m checking the exact observation contract and inherited experiments for a compatible redirect mechanism rather than repeating either edit.

The shelf’s C-start/half-cycle transfer is now influencing the candidate: the useful invariant is to create redirect moment by phase-shaping the measured joint-state rhythm while retaining the 7° mean bend. Because the prior toward-bend booster worsened saturation and closest approach, I’m reading the source-family notes and inherited “away-half-cycle brake” proposal before choosing a bounded version; published gains and timing will not transfer.

The inherited brake proposal has a completed result, so the shelf does not justify adopting it: it still exited low, reached only `2.501L`, and did not beat the `2.443L` parent. Together with the `2.494L` full-direction result, that rules out both post-pass sensing repair alone and the sampled away-half-cycle brake; I’m pruning those from the design space and checking the remaining completed mechanisms before drafting a genuinely different candidate.

The remaining evidence supports one distinct architecture: steer the mean bend from full target direction minus the fish’s measured body-frame course angle, while removing the beat-scale yaw-rate path. This translates the shelf’s direction-tracking/slip invariant into the available normalized observations. It should act before the `17.87T` pass, unlike the failed post-pass fix, and it preserves the proven 7° carrier and posterior gate. I’m recording that falsifiable hypothesis before editing the candidate, as required.

The candidate now implements the single new course-tracking mechanism while retaining the supported carrier and full-direction posterior gate. I’m updating the durable guidance with the completed negative evidence: full-direction gating, distance-only energy relief, and anterior return braking all preserved the same lower-exit topology, so later workers should not treat any of them as sufficient post-pass fixes.

The provenance note and durable guidance are complete. I’m invoking the prescribed check runner now: first the semantic guidance check, then the Julia contract/schema check, then the workspace boundary check. No CFD will be run.

The first prescribed check exposed a rendered-workspace defect rather than a guidance-content failure: `README.md` marks the same guidance parent twice, so the checker counts two copied parents. I’m resolving that duplicate parent marker minimally inside this workspace, then rerunning the required check; this does not alter solver physics or candidate evidence.

All three prescribed checks now pass: semantic guidance, Julia policy contract, and editable-boundary validation. I’m doing one final deterministic audit of parameter-field coverage and file scope, including the non-empty single candidate requirement, before handing off.

Produced exactly one target-policy candidate:

- [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_3d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl) — full-direction, body-frame course-error steering that separates mean curvature from tailbeat-scale yaw.
- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md) — visual diagnosis, inherited negative results, bookshelf transfer block, and falsification criteria.
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md) — reusable lessons covering failed post-pass fixes and beat-contaminated yaw feedback.

All prescribed checks pass: guidance semantics, Julia policy/schema contract, and workspace boundary. No CFD was run. I also removed a duplicated parent marker in `README.md` that initially prevented the required guidance checker from identifying the assigned parent.
